{{article game navigation}} : ''{{Hatnote|You may also be looking for [[Rune (Historical)]], a retired feature of the game.}}'' [[File:Runes 2018.jpg|thumb|360px]]'''Runes''' are enhancements that add new abilities or buffs to the champion. The player can choose their loadout of runes before the match begins, during champion select, or their Collection tab. Runes Reforged (the current system of runes) was introduced in Pre-[[Season 2018]], supplanting the previous system of [[Runes (Historical)|Runes]] and [[Summoner Mastery|Masteries]], hence the name '''Reforged'''.[https://web.archive.org/web/0/http://na.leagueoflegends.com/en/featured/preseason-update Preseason Update][https://web.archive.org/web/0/https://na.leagueoflegends.com/en/news/game-updates/patch/patch-722-notes#patch-experience Patch 7.22 notes][https://web.archive.org/web/0/http://na.leagueoflegends.com/en/featured/preseason-update/8200-8230 Check out my build] == Rune Pages == [[File:Rune_pages_inventory.jpg|thumb|right|400px|Rune page inventory]] A player can have a maximum of 25 custom [[Rune Book|rune pages]], which are separate from the recommended rune page which cannot be edited and only exists per-game. Players in [[Experience (summoner)| levels 1 to 9]] cannot create nor edit rune pages. New accounts have two empty rune pages available; additional pages are purchased in the store for {{RP|590}} or {{BE|6300}} each. It is not possible to enter a match without an active, valid rune page. In such a case, the game will automatically assign the player with the recommended rune page for their champion and role, upon game start. {{clr}} === Rune Recommender === [[File:Rune recommender.png|thumb|right|350px|Rune recommender]] Hovering or locking in a champion in the Champion Selection screen allows you to access the Rune Recommender button on the left side of the loadout. The Rune Recommender automatically determines and recommends the best rune sets for your chosen champion and role, and presents up to three different sets. You can select a set in order to apply it to your loadout. * These recommended rune sets are updated per-patch based on current data and the best runes available for each champion in each role. * Optionally, the Rune Recommender can also recommend [[Summoner spell|summoner spell]] loadouts. The option can be enabled or disabled at will by clicking on the slider at the bottom of the Rune Recommender (this option persists through Champion Selection lobbies). {{clr}} == Rune paths == Runes are divided into five ''paths'': [[File:Rune icon.png|right|100px]] * [[File:Precision icon.png|20px|link=]] '''Precision''' - Improved attacks and sustained damage * [[File:Domination icon.png|20px|link=]] '''Domination''' - Burst damage and target access * [[File:Sorcery icon.png|20px|link=]] '''Sorcery''' - Empowered abilities and resource manipulation * [[File:Resolve icon.png|20px|link=]] '''Resolve''' - Durability and crowd control * [[File:Inspiration icon.png|20px|link=]] '''Inspiration''' - Creative tools and rule bending [[File:In-Game Runes.png|thumb|right|250px]] Each rune page contains runes from two paths: one primary and one secondary. The primary path has one keystone and three lesser runes. The secondary path has two lesser runes. There are also three ''Shard'' slots alongside the Primary and Secondary paths that follow a path separate from the five. Client descriptions may contain unresolved runtime placeholders. Their exact text and the full wiki revisions are retained; no numeric effect is inferred from them.

The scaling-health shard's client description gives 10–180 health, while the Rune article's shard formula is 10 times level through level 20 (200 health). Both sources are retained without choosing a combat value.
The Rune article records champion and game-mode substitutions. Structural page validation does not apply these contextual replacements or certify a page for a particular champion.
Rune effects that depend on elapsed game time, preduel stacks, takedowns, farm, allies, wards, structures or summoner spells require explicit assumptions and source-backed implementation before use.
